docs.title: co: Covariance and coherence matrix estimation (CLI)
docs.text:
Commands of moraine.cli.co (source); the same functions are called in Python as mc.<name>(...) with import moraine.cli as mc. The help below is generated from the docstrings, like moraine COMMAND --help.

command summary emperical-co-pc estimate emperical coherence matrix on point cloud data.

docs.title: emperical-co-pc
docs.text:
estimate emperical coherence matrix on point cloud data.

moraine emperical-co-pc --rslc STR --is_shp_dir STR --gix STR --coh_dir STR [--n_looks_dir STR] [--image_pairs FILE] [--chunks INT INT] [--cuda | --no-cuda] [--processes VALUE] [--n_workers VALUE] [--threads_per_worker VALUE]
argument type default description --rslc str required input rslc stack, shape (nlines, width, nimages) --is_shp_dir str required input directory with the SHP bool arrays of the points, one zarr per raster chunk, made by ras2pc_ras_chunk --gix str required input grid index of the point cloud (azimuth, range), shape (n_points, 2), int --coh_dir str required output directory with the complex coherence of the image pairs of the points, shape (n_points, n_image_pairs), one zarr per raster chunk; merge with pc_concat and the key of ras2pc_ras_chunk --n_looks_dir str None output directory with the effective number of independent looks of the SHP set of each point, float32, shape (n_points,), one zarr per raster chunk (merge as coh_dir): the number of independent looks with the same variance of the coherence estimate as the correlated SHPs, from their positions and the speckle correlation of rslc; input n_looks of ds-temp-coh --image_pairs np.ndarray None input image pairs (element in the coherence matrix) to be calculated, all image pairs by default --chunks tuple[int, int] None parallel processing (azimuth, range) chunk size. Default: rslc.chunks[:2] --cuda bool False if use cuda for processing, false by default --processes None use processes (True) or threads (False) for the workers, only for cpu processing. Default: False --n_workers None number of workers. Default: 1 for cpu, one per GPU for cuda --threads_per_worker None tasks a worker runs at the same time. Default: 2

Global options: --json, --traceback, --log FILE, -q / --quiet (conventions).

In a pipeline (not used by the example pipelines; required arguments only):

[[step]]
name = "emperical_co_pc"
run = "emperical-co-pc"
rslc = "..."
is_shp_dir = "..."
gix = "..."
coh_dir = "..."

In Python:

import moraine.cli as mc
mc.emperical_co_pc(rslc, is_shp_dir, gix, coh_dir, n_looks_dir=None, image_pairs=None, chunks=None, cuda=False, processes=None, n_workers=None, threads_per_worker=None)

The array function mr.emperical_co_pc does the same on numpy / cupy arrays in memory.

docs.title: dl: Deep learning operators (CLI)
docs.text:
Commands of moraine.cli.dl (source); the same functions are called in Python as mc.<name>(...) with import moraine.cli as mc. The help below is generated from the docstrings, like moraine COMMAND --help.

command summary n2f Noise2Fringe (n2f) filtering of raster interferograms n2ft Noise2Fringe Transformer (n2ft) filtering of point cloud interferograms

docs.title: n2f
docs.text:
Noise2Fringe (n2f) filtering of raster interferograms. With cuda the network runs in half precision. A task filters one output chunk with all image pairs: it holds the rslc of one processing chunk with its overlap for all images (8 bytes per pixel and image), the filtered interferograms of the output chunk (8 bytes per pixel and image pair) and the model's activations of one interferogram (about 1 kB per pixel of the processing chunk on the GPU, 2 kB on the CPU); with cuda all of it on the GPU. A worker runs threads_per_worker tasks at a time.

moraine n2f --rslc STR --intf STR --image_pairs FILE [--chunks INT INT] [--out_chunks INT INT] [--depths INT INT] [--model STR] [--cuda | --no-cuda] [--processes VALUE] [--n_workers VALUE] [--threads_per_worker VALUE]
argument type default description --rslc str required input rslc stack, shape (nlines, width, nimages) --intf str required output filtered interferograms, complex64 with unit amplitude (nan where the input is nan), shape (nlines, width, n_image_pairs) --image_pairs np.ndarray required input image pairs (reference, secondary), shape (n_image_pairs, 2); make a file with moraine image-pairs --chunks tuple[int, int] None (azimuth, range) processing chunk size, same as rslc by default; the processing chunks are cut at the output chunks --out_chunks tuple[int, int] None (azimuth, range) chunk size of the output, same as rslc by default; it sets the memory of a worker --depths tuple[int, int], 0) (0, 0) (azimuth, range) overlap in pixels between processing chunks, reduces chunk border effects --model str None path to the model weights (.pth), use the model comes with this package by default --cuda bool False if use cuda for processing, false by default --processes None use processes (True) or threads (False) for the workers, only for cpu processing. Default: True --n_workers None number of workers. Default: 1 for cpu, one per GPU for cuda --threads_per_worker None output chunks a worker filters at the same time. Default: 1

Global options: --json, --traceback, --log FILE, -q / --quiet (conventions).

In a pipeline (examples/02_ps.toml, step n2f):

[[step]]
name = "n2f"                      # Noise2Fringe filtering of the sequential interferograms
run = "n2f"
rslc = "raw/rslc.zarr"
intf = "ps/ras_n2f_intf.zarr"
image_pairs = "ps/pairs_seq.txt"

In Python:

import moraine.cli as mc
mc.n2f(rslc, intf, image_pairs, chunks=None, out_chunks=None, depths=(0, 0), model=None, cuda=False, processes=None, n_workers=None, threads_per_worker=None)

The array function mr.n2f does the same on numpy / cupy arrays in memory.

docs.title: n2ft
docs.text:
Noise2Fringe Transformer (n2ft) filtering of point cloud interferograms. Every worker filters one output chunk of points with all image pairs at a time: it holds the rslc of the points of the chunk and of their halos for the images of the pairs (8 bytes per point and image), the filtered interferograms of the chunk (8 bytes per point and image pair) and about 400 bytes per point of the chunk more; with cuda a model call holds about a fifth of the GPU memory. Before, the main process finds the halos of all processing chunks with about 70 bytes per point and 32 threads of 16 x k x chunks bytes (41 MB each by default).

moraine n2ft --x STR --y STR --rslc STR --intf STR --image_pairs FILE [--chunks VALUE] [--out_chunks VALUE] [--k VALUE] [--model STR] [--cuda | --no-cuda] [--compile | --no-compile] [--processes VALUE] [--n_workers VALUE] [--threads_per_worker VALUE]
argument type default description --x str required input x coordinate of the points (e.g. longitude or easting), shape (n_points,) --y str required input y coordinate of the points (e.g. latitude or northing), shape (n_points,) --rslc str required input rslc of the points, shape (n_points, nimages) --intf str required output filtered interferograms, complex64 with unit amplitude, shape (n_points, n_image_pairs) --image_pairs np.ndarray required input image pairs (reference, secondary), shape (n_image_pairs, 2); make a file with moraine image-pairs --chunks int None number of points per processing chunk, same as rslc by default; the processing chunks do not cross the output chunks --out_chunks int None point chunk size of the output, same as rslc by default; it sets the memory of a worker --k int 128 number of nearest neighbours of every point of a processing chunk that are filtered with it (halo) --model str None path to the model weights (.pth), use the model comes with this package by default --cuda bool False if use cuda for processing, false by default --compile bool None compile the model with torch.compile in every worker: the model then runs about 3 times faster on a GPU, but the compilation takes 15-40 s per worker (less when torch has cached it on disk). Default: when points times image pairs is at least 1e8 --processes None use processes (True) or threads (False) for the workers, only for cpu processing. Default: True --n_workers None number of workers. Default: 1 for cpu, one per GPU for cuda --threads_per_worker None tasks a worker runs at the same time. Default: 1

Global options: --json, --traceback, --log FILE, -q / --quiet (conventions).

In a pipeline (examples/04_refine.toml, step n2ft):

[[step]]
name = "n2ft"                     # Noise2Fringe Transformer filtering of the sequential interferograms
run = "n2ft"
x = "pc/pc_can_lon.zarr"
y = "pc/pc_can_lat.zarr"
rslc = "pc/pc_can_ph.zarr"
intf = "pc/pc_can_n2ft_intf.zarr"
image_pairs = "pc/pairs_seq.txt"
chunks = 20000

In Python:

import moraine.cli as mc
mc.n2ft(x, y, rslc, intf, image_pairs, chunks=None, out_chunks=None, k=128, model=None, cuda=False, compile=None, processes=None, n_workers=None, threads_per_worker=None)

The array function mr.n2ft does the same on numpy / cupy arrays in memory.

docs.title: load-gamma-flatten-rslc
docs.text:
Generate flatten rslc data from gamma command and convert them into zarr format. The shape of hgt should be same as one rslc image, i.e. the hgt file is generated with 1 by 1 look geocoding. All data equal to 0 are replaced with nan.

moraine load-gamma-flatten-rslc --rslc_dir STR --reference STR --hgt STR --scratch_dir STR --rslc STR [--chunks INT INT] [--gamma_threads VALUE] [--processes | --no-processes] [--n_workers VALUE] [--threads_per_worker VALUE]
argument type default description --rslc_dir str required input GAMMA rslc directory with '????????.rslc' and '????????.rslc.par' files --reference str required reference date, eg: '20200202' --hgt str required input DEM height in radar coordinates (GAMMA float), same size as one rslc --scratch_dir str required directory for preserve gamma intermediate files --rslc str required output flattened rslc stack, shape (nlines, width, nimages), complex64 --chunks tuple[int, int], 1000) (1000, 1000) rslc chunk size --gamma_threads int, number of CPU cores) 4 number of threads of each GAMMA program run for an image (phase_sim_orb, set with OMP_NUM_THREADS) --processes False use processes for the workers instead of threads --n_workers 1 number of workers --threads_per_worker 1 tasks a worker runs at the same time

Global options: --json, --traceback, --log FILE, -q / --quiet (conventions).

In a pipeline (examples/01_load.toml, step rslc):

[[step]]
name = "rslc"
run = "load-gamma-flatten-rslc"
rslc_dir = "${gamma}/rslc"
reference = "${reference}"
hgt = "${gamma}/geocoding/${geo}.hgt"
scratch_dir = "raw/scratch"
rslc = "raw/rslc.zarr"

In Python:

import moraine.cli as mc
mc.load_gamma_flatten_rslc(rslc_dir, reference, hgt, scratch_dir, rslc, chunks=(1000, 1000), gamma_threads=4, processes=False, n_workers=1, threads_per_worker=1)

docs.title: math
docs.text:
Basic math manipulation. Only elementwise operations are supported. Only one output is supported.

moraine math --output STR --operation STR [--kw KEY=VALUE]
argument type default description --output str required output path of the result, same shape and chunks as the inputs --operation str required numexpr expression of the input arrays, e.g. 'sin(a)*exp(b)/2' --kw KEY=VALUE extra keyword argument, repeatable: input: the arrays used in operation as NAME=zarr path, e.g. a='a.zarr' (on the command line: --kw a=a.zarr)

Global options: --json, --traceback, --log FILE, -q / --quiet (conventions).

In a pipeline (not used by the example pipelines; required arguments only):

[[step]]
name = "math"
run = "math"
output = "..."
operation = "..."

In Python:

import moraine.cli as mc
mc.math(output, operation, **data)

docs.title: pl: Phase linking (CLI)
docs.text:
Commands of moraine.cli.pl (source); the same functions are called in Python as mc.<name>(...) with import moraine.cli as mc. The help below is generated from the docstrings, like moraine COMMAND --help.

command summary emi Phase linking with EMI estimator. ds-temp-coh DS temporal coherence, optionally also weighted by the coherence of the image pairs. emperical-co-emi-temp-coh-pc estimating emperical coherence matrix, phase linking and estimating temporal coherence on point cloud data.

docs.title: emi
docs.text:
Phase linking with EMI estimator.

moraine emi --coh STR --ph STR [--ref VALUE] [--regularize | --no-regularize] [--chunks INT INT] [--cuda | --no-cuda] [--processes VALUE] [--n_workers VALUE] [--threads_per_worker VALUE]
argument type default description --coh str required input complex coherence of the points (upper triangle of the coherence matrix), shape (n_points, n_image_pairs) --ph str required output phase history of the points, complex, shape (n_points, nimages) --ref int 0 index of the reference image, its phase is set to 0 --regularize bool True regularize the coherence matrix of the points whose coherence magnitude matrix is not positive definite or numerically singular (e.g. when the number of images approaches the number of independent looks of the SHPs; without it their phase history is not reliable); points with a well conditioned positive definite matrix are not changed --chunks int None point chunk size of the output data, same as coh by default --cuda bool False if use cuda for processing, false by default --processes None use processes (True) or threads (False) for the workers, only for cpu processing. Default: False --n_workers None number of workers. Default: 1 for cpu, one per GPU for cuda --threads_per_worker None tasks a worker runs at the same time. Default: 2

Global options: --json, --traceback, --log FILE, -q / --quiet (conventions).

In a pipeline (not used by the example pipelines; required arguments only):

[[step]]
name = "emi"
run = "emi"
coh = "..."
ph = "..."

In Python:

import moraine.cli as mc
mc.emi(coh, ph, ref=0, regularize=True, chunks=None, cuda=False, processes=None, n_workers=None, threads_per_worker=None)

The array function mr.emi does the same on numpy / cupy arrays in memory.

docs.title: ds-temp-coh
docs.text:
DS temporal coherence, optionally also weighted by the coherence of the image pairs.

moraine ds-temp-coh --coh STR --ph STR [--t_coh STR] [--tnet STR] [--n_looks STR] [--t_coh_w STR] [--eff_n_pairs STR] [--n_components STR] [--alpha VALUE] [--chunks INT INT] [--cuda | --no-cuda] [--processes VALUE] [--n_workers VALUE] [--threads_per_worker VALUE]
argument type default description --coh str required input complex coherence of the points (upper triangle of the coherence matrix), shape (n_points, n_image_pairs) --ph str required input phase history of the points, complex, shape (n_points, nimages) --t_coh str None output temporal coherence of the points, every image pair weighted the same, shape (n_points,) --tnet str None input path of a saved TempNet with the image pairs of coh; all image pairs by default --n_looks str None input effective number of independent looks of the coherence of the points, float32, shape (n_points,), in the order of coh: the merged n_looks_dir of emperical-co-pc; needed by t_coh_w and eff_n_pairs --t_coh_w str None output weighted temporal coherence of the points, float32, shape (n_points,), 0..1: the image pairs weighted by their squared coherence without the noise bias, so that incoherent pairs (e.g. long time spans in vegetation) do not lower it; NaN where no image pair is above the noise level --eff_n_pairs str None output effective number of image pairs the weighted temporal coherence rests on, float32, shape (n_points,), 0..n_image_pairs; a high weighted temporal coherence of few effective pairs is not reliable --n_components str None output number of connected components of the graph whose nodes are the images and whose edges are the coherent image pairs, int16, shape (n_points,), 1..nimages; 1 means every image is linked to every other by coherent pairs, with more the phase between the groups of images is not constrained by any coherent pair, whatever the weighted temporal coherence is; needs n_looks --alpha float 0.001 probability that a point without any coherent image pair (pure noise) has all images connected (n_components 1); it sets the squared coherence above which an image pair counts as coherent, depending on the number of looks and of images; 1e-6 <= alpha <= 0.5; only with n_looks --chunks int None point cloud chunk size, same as coh by default --cuda bool False if use cuda for processing, false by default --processes None use processes (True) or threads (False) for the workers, only for cpu processing. Default: False --n_workers None number of workers. Default: 1 for cpu, one per GPU for cuda --threads_per_worker None tasks a worker runs at the same time. Default: 2

Global options: --json, --traceback, --log FILE, -q / --quiet (conventions).

coh = "..."
ph = "..."

docs.title: emperical-co-emi-temp-coh-pc
docs.text:
estimating emperical coherence matrix, phase linking and estimating temporal coherence on point cloud data.

moraine emperical-co-emi-temp-coh-pc --rslc STR --is_shp_dir STR --gix STR --ph_dir STR --t_coh_dir STR [--t_coh_w_dir STR] [--eff_n_pairs_dir STR] [--n_components_dir STR] [--alpha VALUE] [--batch_size VALUE] [--regularize | --no-regularize] [--chunks INT INT] [--cuda | --no-cuda] [--processes VALUE] [--n_workers VALUE] [--threads_per_worker VALUE]
argument type default description --rslc str required input rslc stack, shape (nlines, width, nimages) --is_shp_dir str required input directory with the SHP bool arrays of the points, one zarr per raster chunk, made by ras2pc_ras_chunk --gix str required input grid index of the point cloud (azimuth, range), shape (n_points, 2), int --ph_dir str required output directory with the phase history of the points, complex, shape (n_points, nimages), one zarr per raster chunk; merge with pc_concat and the key of ras2pc_ras_chunk --t_coh_dir str required output directory with the temporal coherence of the points, shape (n_points,), one zarr per raster chunk --t_coh_w_dir str None output directory with the weighted temporal coherence of the points (see ds-temp-coh), shape (n_points,), float32, 0..1, NaN where no image pair is above the noise level, one zarr per raster chunk; the effective number of looks of each point comes from the positions of its SHPs and the speckle correlation of rslc --eff_n_pairs_dir str None output directory with the effective number of image pairs of the weighted temporal coherence, shape (n_points,), float32, one zarr per raster chunk; a high weighted temporal coherence of few effective pairs is not reliable --n_components_dir str None output directory with the number of connected components of the graph whose nodes are the images and whose edges are the coherent image pairs (see ds-temp-coh), shape (n_points,), int16, 1..nimages, one zarr per raster chunk; 1 means every image is linked to every other by coherent pairs --alpha float 0.001 probability that a point without any coherent image pair (pure noise) has all images connected; 1e-6 <= alpha <= 0.5; see ds-temp-coh; only with one of the weighted outputs --batch_size int None number of points a worker processes at once; the coherence matrices of a batch take 8 bytes per image pair and point, their estimation on the GPU up to 1 GiB more. Default: as many points as 1 GiB of coherence matrices hold (small batches cost time: thousands of small GPU operations per batch) --regularize bool True regularize the coherence matrix in the phase linking as regularize of emi; the temporal coherence is computed with the coherence matrix as estimated --chunks tuple[int, int] None parallel processing (azimuth, range) chunk size. Default: rslc.chunks[:2] --cuda bool False if use cuda for processing, false by default --processes None use processes (True) or threads (False) for the workers, only for cpu processing. Default: False --n_workers None number of workers. Default: 1 for cpu, one per GPU for cuda --threads_per_worker None tasks a worker runs at the same time. Default: 2

docs.text:
render raster data to pyramid of difference zoom levels.

moraine ras-pyramid --ras STR --out_dir STR [--chunks INT INT] [--rows VALUE] [--method STR] [--n_workers VALUE]
argument type default description --ras str required input 2D raster (nlines, width) or raster stack (nlines, width, n) --out_dir str required output directory to store rendered data --chunks tuple[int, int], 256) (256, 256) output raster tile size --rows int 1024 lines of the raster a process reads at a time, a power of 2; a process needs about 1 GB plus 3 x rows x width x itemsize bytes --method str 'decimate' how each level is made from the finer one: 'decimate' keeps every 2nd pixel, 'mean' averages the 2 x 2 blocks (nan pixels left out, complex data as complex numbers; integer and boolean data give float32 levels). command summary polygon-mask Mask of the pixels or points inside (or outside) the polygons of a GeoJSON file

docs.title: polygon-mask
docs.text:
Mask of the pixels or points inside (or outside) the polygons of a GeoJSON file. The polygons come from the tile viewer (TileView.save_polygons) or any GeoJSON file. Give the positions of the data in the coordinates of the file in one of three ways: x and y (longitude / latitude for 'lonlat' files, range / azimuth for 'radar_grid' files), gix (point clouds on the radar grid) or shape (a whole raster on the radar grid, pixel (i, j) at range j, azimuth i). Apply the mask with e.g. math (where(mask, a, nan)) or pc-logic-pc.

moraine polygon-mask --polygons STR --mask STR [--x STR] [--y STR] [--gix STR] [--shape INT INT] [--keep STR] [--chunks INT INT]
argument type default description --polygons str required input GeoJSON file with the polygons --mask str required output bool mask, True for the data to keep; same shape as x / y, (n_points,) for gix, (nlines, width) for shape --x str None input x coordinate of the data (longitude or range), any shape; with y --y str None input y coordinate of the data (latitude or azimuth), same shape as x --gix str None input grid index (azimuth, range) of a point cloud, shape (n_points, 2); 'radar_grid' polygons only --shape tuple[int, int] None raster shape (nlines, width); 'radar_grid' polygons only --keep str 'inside' 'inside' keeps the data inside any polygon (True there), 'outside' keeps the data outside all polygons --chunks tuple[int, int], 1000) (1000, 1000) output chunk size for shape; the other outputs are chunked like their input

docs.title: mcf-pc
docs.text:
Minimum cost flow phase unwrapping of point cloud interferograms. Every interferogram is unwrapped alone on the Delaunay network of the points. The network stays in memory, about 50 bytes per point (100 with spatial_cost 'length'), and every interferogram unwrapped at the same time needs about 160 bytes per point more.

moraine mcf-pc --gix STR --ph STR --unw_ph STR --image_pairs FILE --range_pixel_spacing VALUE --azimuth_pixel_spacing VALUE [--earth_cost VALUE] [--spatial_cost STR] [--n_workers VALUE] [--out_chunks VALUE]
argument type default description --gix str required input grid index (azimuth, range) of the points, shape (n_points, 2), int; the points must be unique --ph str required input wrapped phase history (complex), shape (n_points, nimages), chunked one image per chunk (points_block, 1) --unw_ph str required output unwrapped phase of the interferograms in radians, shape (n_points, n_pairs), float32, chunks (out_chunks, 1); the first point keeps its wrapped phase --image_pairs np.ndarray required image pairs (reference, secondary) of the interferograms to unwrap, shape (n_pairs, 2); the interferogram is reference * conj(secondary) --range_pixel_spacing float required range pixel spacing in meters --azimuth_pixel_spacing float required azimuth pixel spacing in meters --earth_cost int 1 cost of a phase jump across the convex hull of the points, relative to 1 inside; a larger value discourages discharging residues through the border --spatial_cost str 'constant' where phase jumps are placed first: 'constant' (anywhere alike) or 'length' (long connections between points) --n_workers int None number of interferograms unwrapped at the same time; by default as many as the available cores and half of the available memory allow --out_chunks int None point chunk size of unw_ph, same as ph by default

Global options: --json, --traceback, --log FILE, -q / --quiet (conventions).

image_pairs = "unw/pairs_seq.txt"

azimuth_pixel_spacing = "${azimuth_pixel_spacing}"

mc.mcf_pc(gix, ph, unw_ph, image_pairs, range_pixel_spacing, azimuth_pixel_spacing, earth_cost=1, spatial_cost='constant', n_workers=None, out_chunks=None)

The array function mr.mcf_pc does the same on numpy / cupy arrays in memory.

docs.title: emcf-pc
docs.text:
Extended minimum cost flow (EMCF) phase unwrapping of point cloud interferograms. The interferograms of a network of image pairs are unwrapped together: the redundancy of the network (image pairs that close loops, e.g. (a, b), (b, c) and (a, c)) is used against unwrapping errors. The coordinates and the network of the points stay in memory, about 120 bytes per point, and every interferogram unwrapped at the same time needs about 200 bytes per point more. Intermediate results are written to unw_ph.tmp (kept if the command fails, removed at the end).

moraine emcf-pc --gix STR --ph STR --image_pairs FILE --unw_ph STR --range_pixel_spacing VALUE --azimuth_pixel_spacing VALUE [--dates PATH [PATH ...]] [--weight STR] [--earth_cost VALUE] [--temporal_cost STR] [--spatial_cost STR] [--n_workers VALUE] [--out_chunks VALUE]
argument type default description --gix str required input grid index (azimuth, range) of the points, shape (n_points, 2), int; the points must be unique --ph str required input wrapped phase history (complex), shape (n_points, nimages), chunked one image per chunk (points_block, 1) --image_pairs np.ndarray required the interferograms: (reference, secondary) image indices, shape (n_pairs, 2), e.g. a file made by image-pairs (--bandwidth 3: every image with the next three); the interferogram is reference * conj(secondary); without any loop in the network every interferogram is unwrapped alone --unw_ph str required output unwrapped phase of the interferograms in radians, shape (n_points, n_pairs), float32, chunks (out_chunks, 1); at the first point the difference of the wrapped phases of the two images. Loops of image pairs may still not add up to zero at some points: see unwrap-correct-closure-pc --range_pixel_spacing float required range pixel spacing in meters --azimuth_pixel_spacing float required azimuth pixel spacing in meters --dates str or list None acquisition date of every image (YYYYMMDD), nimages values; needed by temporal_cost 'length' --weight str None input quality of the points from 0 (unreliable) to 1, e.g. the temporal coherence, shape (n_points,); needed by spatial_cost 'weight' --earth_cost int 1 cost of a phase jump across the border of the network of points, relative to 1 inside; a larger value discourages discharging residues through the border --temporal_cost str 'constant' which interferograms are corrected first where the interferograms of a loop of image pairs disagree: 'constant' (all alike) or 'length' (the longest in time) --spatial_cost str 'constant' where phase jumps are placed first in every interferogram: 'constant' (anywhere alike), 'length' (long connections between points), 'weight' (points of low weight) or 'length+weight' --n_workers int None number of interferograms unwrapped at the same time; by default as many as the available cores and half of the available memory allow --out_chunks int None point chunk size of unw_ph, same as ph by default

Global options: --json, --traceback, --log FILE, -q / --quiet (conventions).

In a pipeline (not used by the example pipelines; required arguments only):

[[step]]

ph = "..."
image_pairs = "..."
unw_ph = "..."
range_pixel_spacing = "..."
azimuth_pixel_spacing = "..."

docs.title: unwrap-correct-closure-pc
docs.text:
Correction of unwrapping errors of point cloud interferograms by phase closure, to the unwrapped phase of every image. The unwrapped phases of every loop of image pairs should add up to zero, e.g. unw(a, b) + unw(b, c) = unw(a, c). Where they do not, the interferograms are corrected by whole cycles, changing as few interferograms as possible, by the same amount for all points of a region: the points connected by edges of the point network no longer than max_edge_factor times the median edge length. Points of smaller regions than min_region_points are corrected one by one. The correction assumes that most interferograms of a region are right: where most are wrong, it makes them worse. Where a point still does not fit the loops after the correction of its region, the interferograms fitting most of its loops are kept. The result is the unwrapped phase of every image, whose differences close every loop. Errors that close every loop (e.g. the same whole cycles in every interferogram of one image) are neither corrected nor reported. The region of every point stays in memory (4 bytes per point; about 100 bytes per point while the regions are made). Intermediate results are written to ts.tmp (kept if the command fails, removed at the end).

moraine unwrap-correct-closure-pc --gix STR --ph STR --unw_ph STR --image_pairs FILE --ts STR --range_pixel_spacing VALUE --azimuth_pixel_spacing VALUE [--ref VALUE] [--misclosure_fraction STR] [--change_fraction STR] [--region STR] [--max_edge_factor VALUE] [--min_region_points VALUE] [--n_workers VALUE] [--out_chunks VALUE]
argument type default description --gix str required input grid index (azimuth, range) of the points, shape (n_points, 2), int; the points must be unique --ph str required input wrapped phase history (complex), shape (n_points, nimages), chunked one image per chunk (points_block, 1) --unw_ph str required input unwrapped phase of the interferograms in radians, shape (n_points, n_pairs), chunked one interferogram per chunk (points_block, 1), e.g. from mcf-pc or emcf-pc; rewrapped, it must be the phase of ph[:, reference] * conj(ph[:, secondary]) --image_pairs np.ndarray required the interferograms: (reference, secondary) image indices of the columns of unw_ph, shape (n_pairs, 2); the pairs must connect all images; the network needs loops (e.g. every image paired with the next three) to correct anything, otherwise only the image phases are computed (a warning is given) --ts str required output unwrapped phase of every image relative to image ref in radians, shape (n_points, nimages), float32, chunks (out_chunks, 1); ts[:, ref] is 0; rewrapped, ts[:, j] is the phase of ph[:, j] * conj(ph[:, ref]); the corrected interferogram (a, b) is ts[:, a] - ts[:, b] --range_pixel_spacing float required range pixel spacing in meters --azimuth_pixel_spacing float required azimuth pixel spacing in meters --ref int 0 index of the reference image, 0 .. nimages - 1: the image phases are relative to it --misclosure_fraction str None output fraction of the interferograms of every point that do not fit the loops before the correction, shape (n_points,), float32, 0..1; 0 where every loop closes --change_fraction str None output fraction of the interferograms of every point whose whole cycles in ts differ from unw_ph, shape (n_points,), float32, 0..1; 0 where unw_ph was kept; large values mark points whose input unwrapping was poor (e.g. to be masked) --region str None output region of every point, shape (n_points,), int32: 0 .. n_regions - 1, or -1 for the points of regions smaller than min_region_points, corrected one by one (e.g. to be masked) --max_edge_factor float 4.0 edges of the point network longer than this times the median edge length do not connect a region, e.g. edges across water or decorrelated areas; larger than 1 --min_region_points int 30 in regions of fewer points every point is corrected by its own loops alone, which is less reliable --n_workers int None number of interferograms corrected at the same time; by default as many as the available cores and half of the available memory allow --out_chunks int None point chunk size of the outputs, same as unw_ph by default

Global options: --json, --traceback, --log FILE, -q / --quiet (conventions).

In a pipeline (not used by the example pipelines; required arguments only):

[[step]]
name = "unwrap_correct_closure_pc"
run = "unwrap-correct-closure-pc"
gix = "..."
ph = "..."
unw_ph = "..."
image_pairs = "..."
ts = "..."
range_pixel_spacing = "..."
azimuth_pixel_spacing = "..."

In Python:

import moraine.cli as mc
mc.unwrap_correct_closure_pc(gix, ph, unw_ph, image_pairs, ts, range_pixel_spacing, azimuth_pixel_spacing, ref=0, misclosure_fraction=None, change_fraction=None, region=None, max_edge_factor=4.0, min_region_points=30, n_workers=None, out_chunks=None)

The array function mr.unwrap_correct_closure_pc does the same on numpy / cupy arrays in memory.

docs.title: shp: Spatially Homogeneous Pixels Identification
docs.text:
Commands of moraine.cli.shp (source); the same functions are called in Python as mc.<name>(...) with import moraine.cli as mc. The help below is generated from the docstrings, like moraine COMMAND --help.

command summary shp-test SHP identification through hypothesis test, and the selection of the SHPs at the level alpha. select-shp Select SHP based on pvalue of SHP test.

docs.title: shp-test
docs.text:
SHP identification through hypothesis test, and the selection of the SHPs at the level alpha.

moraine shp-test --rslc STR --is_shp STR --shp_num STR --az_half_win VALUE --r_half_win VALUE [--alpha VALUE] [--pvalue STR] [--method STR] [--chunks INT INT] [--cuda | --no-cuda] [--processes VALUE] [--n_workers VALUE] [--threads_per_worker VALUE]
argument type default description --rslc str required input rslc stack, shape (nlines, width, nimages) --is_shp str required output True for the SHPs of each pixel, i.e. the pixels of its window whose p value is at least alpha, shape (nlines, width, 2az_half_win+1, 2r_half_win+1), bool --shp_num str required output number of SHPs of each pixel, shape (nlines, width), int32 --az_half_win int required azimuth half window size --r_half_win int required range half window size --alpha float 0.05 significance level of the test, in (0, 1): a pixel is an SHP of the centre pixel of its window when its p value is at least alpha; a larger alpha keeps fewer SHPs --pvalue str None output p value of the test between each pixel and the pixels in its window, same shape as is_shp, float32; needed only to select the SHPs again at another level with select-shp --method str None test method, only 'ks' (two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov) is implemented. Default: 'ks' --chunks tuple[int, int] None (azimuth, range) processing chunk size, same as rslc by default --cuda bool False if use cuda for processing, false by default --processes None use processes (True) or threads (False) for the workers, only for cpu processing. Default: False --n_workers None number of workers. Default: 1 for cpu, one per GPU for cuda --threads_per_worker None tasks a worker runs at the same time. Default: 1

Global options: --json, --traceback, --log FILE, -q / --quiet (conventions).

In a pipeline (examples/03_ds.toml, step shp_test):

[[step]]
name = "shp_test"                 # two sample KS test in a 7 x 27 window (about 100 m x 60 m on the ground), SHPs = p value >= alpha
run = "shp-test"
rslc = "raw/rslc.zarr"
az_half_win = 3
r_half_win = 13
is_shp = "ds/ras_is_shp.zarr"
shp_num = "ds/ras_shp_num.zarr"
alpha = 0.05                      # significance level; add pvalue = "ds/ras_pvalue.zarr" to keep the p values

In Python:

import moraine.cli as mc
mc.shp_test(rslc, is_shp, shp_num, az_half_win, r_half_win, alpha=0.05, pvalue=None, method=None, chunks=None, cuda=False, processes=None, n_workers=None, threads_per_worker=None)

docs.title: select-shp
docs.text:
Select SHP based on pvalue of SHP test.

moraine select-shp --pvalue STR --is_shp STR --shp_num STR [--alpha VALUE] [--chunks INT INT] [--processes | --no-processes] [--n_workers VALUE] [--threads_per_worker VALUE]
argument type default description --pvalue str required input pvalue of hypothesis test --is_shp str required output bool array, True for SHPs, same shape as pvalue --shp_num str required output number of SHPs of each pixel, shape (nlines, width), int32 --alpha float 0.05 significance level of the test, in (0, 1): a pixel is an SHP of the centre pixel of its window when its p value is at least alpha, i.e. the test does not reject that both have the same distribution; a larger alpha keeps fewer SHPs --chunks tuple[int, int] None (azimuth, range) processing chunk size, same as pvalue by default --processes False use processes for the workers instead of threads, the default is False --n_workers 1 number of workers, the default is 1 --threads_per_worker 1 tasks a worker runs at the same time

Global options: --json, --traceback, --log FILE, -q / --quiet (conventions).

In a pipeline (not used by the example pipelines; required arguments only):

[[step]]
name = "select_shp"
run = "select-shp"
pvalue = "..."
is_shp = "..."
shp_num = "..."

In Python:

import moraine.cli as mc
mc.select_shp(pvalue, is_shp, shp_num, alpha=0.05, chunks=None, processes=False, n_workers=1, threads_per_worker=1)

The array function mr.select_shp does the same on numpy / cupy arrays in memory.

docs.title: transform: transform coordinate between projection
docs.text:
Commands of moraine.cli.transform (source); the same functions are called in Python as mc.<name>(...) with import moraine.cli as mc. The help below is generated from the docstrings, like moraine COMMAND --help.

command summary transform Coordinate transformation

docs.title: transform
docs.text:
Coordinate transformation. By default, the input should be longitude (xx_in) and latitude (yy_in) (in degree) and outputs are x (east) and y (south) coordinate in web mercator projection (for plot with google earth map). The chunks, shape and dtype of output are same as xx_in.

moraine transform --xx_in VALUE --yy_in VALUE --xx_out VALUE --yy_out VALUE [--epsg_in VALUE] [--epsg_out VALUE]
argument type default description --xx_in required input x coordinate (longitude in degree for the default epsg_in) --yy_in required input y coordinate (latitude in degree for the default epsg_in) --xx_out required output x coordinate in epsg_out, same shape and chunks as xx_in --yy_out required output y coordinate in epsg_out, same shape and chunks as xx_in --epsg_in int 4326 EPSG code of the input coordinates (4326: WGS84 longitude/latitude) --epsg_out int 3857 EPSG code of the output coordinates (3857: web mercator)

Global options: --json, --traceback, --log FILE, -q / --quiet (conventions).

In a pipeline (examples/01_load.toml, step web_mercator):

[[step]]
name = "web_mercator"             # e/n coordinates, used to plot point clouds on a map
run = "transform"
xx_in = "raw/lon.zarr"
yy_in = "raw/lat.zarr"
xx_out = "raw/e.zarr"
yy_out = "raw/n.zarr"

In Python:

import moraine.cli as mc
mc.transform(xx_in, yy_in, xx_out, yy_out, epsg_in=4326, epsg_out=3857)

docs.title: Contracts
docs.text:
Formats and behaviour that users, scripts, agents or other moraine versions depend on. A contract is a promise: when the code and a contract disagree, the code is wrong, unless a new contract version is released on purpose. tests/test_contracts.py checks the code against them.

contract version where the version is JSON output of moraine ... --json 1 version field of every output; moraine.command.JSON_VERSION Pipeline files run by moraine run 1 optional [pipeline] version; moraine.command.pipeline.PIPELINE_VERSION Pyramids made by ras-pyramid / pc-pyramid 1 moraine_pyramid attribute of 0.zarr; moraine.cli.plot.PYRAMID_VERSION Data conventions of arrays and zarr datasets - changes need a decision record

docs.title: Changing a contract
docs.text:
• Compatible additions (a new optional field, a new optional table key) keep the version; document them here and in the tests in the same change.
  • Anything that breaks existing files, scripts or readers (renamed or removed fields, changed meaning, changed layout) bumps the version, keeps reading the old version where possible, and needs a decision record in docs/decisions/.
  • Update CHANGELOG.md for every contract change.

docs.title: Contract: data conventions
docs.text: Shapes, orders and meanings of the arrays moraine functions and commands exchange. Changing them needs a decision record, since every stored result depends on them.

docs.title: Rasters
docs.text:
• Shape (nlines, width[, n]): azimuth (lines) first, range second, stacks last.
  • rslc stack: (nlines, width, nimages) complex64, images in date order.
  • nan marks missing data.

docs.title: Chunks
docs.text:
Decision 0019.

  • Stacks are chunked in space by blocks and along the image (or image pair) axis with one image per chunk: point clouds (n_points, nimages) as (points_block, 1), rasters (nlines, width, nimages) as (lines_block, width_block, 1); the same for interferograms, coherence and unwrapped phase (n_points, n_pairs).
  • Arrays without an image axis are chunked in space only: (points_block,), (points_block, 2) for gix, (lines_block, width_block).
  • Window arrays (the p values and SHP flags of the SHP test, (nlines, width, az_win, r_win), and their point cloud form (n_points, az_win, r_win)) are chunked in space only, with the whole window of a pixel in one chunk: (lines_block, width_block, az_win, r_win), (points_block, az_win, r_win) (decision 0032).
  • A step per image (or image pair) then reads and writes whole chunks, and a step per block of points or pixels reads one chunk of every image, without rechunking. Temporary zarrs between the steps of a command follow the same layout.
  • Commands expect this layout and report other chunks instead of rechunking them.

docs.title: Point clouds
docs.text:
• Arrays of shape (n_points, ...), the first axis indexes the points.
  • gix: grid index (n_points, 2) int32, (azimuth, range) of each point in its raster.
  • hix: hilbert index (n_points,) int64 of the grid index, computed with the raster shape.
  • Point clouds are kept in hilbert order (pc-sort), so points close in the array are close on the ground. pc-union, pc-intersect, pc-diff and pc-select-data require sorted indices.
  • Commands working per raster chunk (ras2pc-ras-chunk, emperical-co-pc, emperical-co-emi-temp-coh-pc) write a directory with one zarr per chunk (0.zarr, 1.zarr, ...), in raster chunk order. pc-concat merges it back, sorted with the key of ras2pc-ras-chunk and, for hilbert order, the key of pc-sort.

docs.title: Interferometric data
docs.text:
• Image pairs (n_pairs, 2) int: (reference, secondary) image index; the interferogram is ref * conj(sec). Image pair files have these two columns.
  • Interferograms and phase histories are complex; the phase is angle(...). Filtered interferograms and phase histories have unit amplitude.
  • Coherence of point clouds is compressed: the upper triangle of the coherence matrix, (n_points, n_pairs) in the order of numpy.triu_indices(nimages, 1) unless image pairs are given; moraine.uncompress_coh restores full matrices.
  • Unwrapped phase: float32 radians, (n_points, n_pairs).
  • Unwrapped phase of the images (phase time series): float32 radians, (n_points, nimages), relative to a reference image whose column is 0; interferogram (a, b) is ts[:, a] - ts[:, b] (decision 0022).

docs.title: Polygons
docs.text:
• GeoJSON files (decision 0017): a FeatureCollection of Polygon (or MultiPolygon) features; only the outer rings are used, several polygons are united.
  • The top level member moraine_coordinates gives the vertex coordinates: lonlat (longitude, latitude in degrees, the GeoJSON default when the member is missing) or radar_grid (range, azimuth pixel coordinates, pixel (i, j) at range j, azimuth i).
  • Masks made from them (polygon-mask) are bool arrays of the shape of the data, True for the data to keep.

docs.title: Contract: JSON output
docs.text:
Version 1. With --json, every moraine command prints exactly one JSON object on stdout (logs and progress bars go to stderr) and exits with 0 on success, 1 on a processing error and 2 on a usage error.

tests/test_contracts.py compares the fields listed here with the real output: required fields must be present, fields marked optional may be missing, other fields must not appear.

docs.title: Every output
docs.text: field type description version integer version of this contract, 1 ok boolean false if the command failed

docs.title: error
docs.text:
Printed instead of the normal output when the command fails (ok is false).

field type description error string the error message

docs.title: processing command
docs.text:
Any command of moraine list (e.g. moraine amp-disp ... --json).

field type description command string command name seconds number run time outputs list of strings argument paths created or modified by the command inputs object argument paths read by the command -> their modification time (ns) summaries list of summaries one summary (see below) per output

docs.title: list
docs.text: field type description commands list of objects name, module (moraine.cli module) and summary (first docstring line) of every command

docs.title: info
docs.text: field type description summaries list of summaries one summary per path argument

docs.title: quicklook
docs.text: field type description png string the PNG written

docs.title: view
docs.text: field type description notebook string the notebook written pyramids list of strings the pyramids it shows, as given

docs.title: run
docs.text:
field type description pipeline string the pipeline file workdir string the working directory plan list of objects per step: name, command, action (run (reason) or skip (reason)) steps list of step records the steps that ran (see below); with --dry-run empty

A failing step stops the run: ok is false, the exit code is 1 and the last step record has status = "failed" and the error; there is no top level error field.

docs.title: status
docs.text: field type description pipeline string the pipeline file workdir string the working directory steps list of objects per step: name, command, status (pending, done, failed, outdated, will run (reason)), and when it ran before seconds, finished, error, log, outputs, quicklooks

docs.title: step record
docs.text:
Items of steps in the run output.

field type description name string step name command string command name hash string hash of the command and its arguments, used to detect changes args object the arguments as written in the pipeline file (after ${var} substitution) started string start time, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS finished string end time log string log file, relative to the working directory status string done or failed seconds number optional, run time (done only) outputs list of strings optional, paths created or modified (done only) inputs object optional, paths read -> modification time (done only) summaries list of summaries optional, summaries of the outputs (done only) quicklooks list of strings optional, PNGs of the pyramid outputs error string optional, the error (failed only)

docs.title: Summaries
docs.text: Objects describing a path (moraine info, outputs of commands and steps). kind tells which one.

docs.title: array summary
docs.text: field type description path string the path kind string array shape list of integers array shape dtype string numpy dtype chunks list of integers zarr chunk shape

docs.title: pyramid summary
docs.text:
kind is raster pyramid or point cloud pyramid (see the pyramid contract). The statistics are those of all the data, computed when the pyramid was built (stats_level 0); for pyramids made without them they come from the finest level of at most 64 MiB (stats_level > 0), point cloud pyramids skipping empty cells. For complex data the value fields are named amplitude_min, amplitude_max, ... and describe the amplitude; for boolean data only true_fraction is given.

field type description path string the path kind string raster pyramid or point cloud pyramid shape list of integers shape of level 0 dtype string numpy dtype of the data (of the points for a point cloud pyramid) levels integer number of levels method string optional, how the levels are made: decimate or mean (rasters), first or mean (point clouds); absent for pyramids made before it existed stats_level integer level used for the statistics, 0 when they are of all the data nan_fraction number optional, fraction of nan values min number optional, minimum (finite values) max number optional, maximum mean number optional, mean std number optional, standard deviation p01 number optional, 1st percentile p50 number optional, median p99 number optional, 99th percentile amplitude_min number optional, as min, for complex data amplitude_max number optional amplitude_mean number optional amplitude_std number optional amplitude_p01 number optional amplitude_p50 number optional amplitude_p99 number optional true_fraction number optional, fraction of true values, for boolean data warnings list of strings optional, anomalies: all values nan, infinite values, constant values; the images or channels of a stack that are all nan or constant

docs.title: directory summary
docs.text: field type description path string the path kind string directory n_zarr integer number of zarr arrays below it zarr list of strings their paths relative to it, at most 20

docs.title: group summary
docs.text: field type description path string the path kind string group members list of strings member names

docs.title: file summary
docs.text: field type description path string the path kind string file bytes integer file size

docs.title: failed summary
docs.text:
A summary that could not be made (the command itself succeeded).

field type description path string the path error string why the summary failed

docs.title: Contract: pipeline files
docs.text: Version 1. TOML files run by moraine run FILE and inspected by moraine status FILE (decision 0006).

docs.title: Tables
docs.text:
table / key required description [pipeline] no settings of the file [pipeline] version no format version, integer, default 1; newer versions than the installed moraine supports are rejected [pipeline] workdir no working directory, relative to the file; default: the directory of the file; --workdir overrides it [pipeline] quicklook no save PNGs of the pyramids made by the steps, default true [vars] no variables; ${name} is replaced in every value of [defaults] and [[step]]; --var name=value overrides [defaults] no arguments given to every step whose command has them [[step]] yes the steps, run in file order name yes unique step name run yes a command of moraine list quicklook no per step override of [pipeline] quicklook kw no table of extra keyword arguments passed to the function (**kwargs), e.g. the input arrays of math any other key - an argument of the command; unknown names are errors

No other top level tables and no other [pipeline] keys are allowed.

docs.title: Values
docs.text:
• Paths are relative to the working directory; each step runs with the working directory as current directory.
  • Booleans, integers, floats and strings are TOML values. Tuples (tuple[int, int] arguments) are TOML lists [1000, 1000] or strings "1000,1000"; their number of integers is checked.
  • Arguments accepting several paths take a TOML list.
  • image_pairs is a file with two integer columns (made by the image-pairs command) or a list of pairs; a file is read when the step runs, so an earlier step may make it.
  • An unknown ${name} is an error.

docs.title: Execution
docs.text:
• Steps run in file order; the first failing step stops the run (exit code 1).
  • A step is skipped when it finished before with the same command and arguments (hash), all its outputs exist and none of its inputs changed (modification time). Otherwise it runs; steps reading the outputs of a step that runs are rerun too. --force, --from STEP and --only STEP override this.
  • --dry-run prints the plan with the reason for each step and runs nothing.
  • Outputs and inputs of a step are the argument paths it created / modified and read.

docs.title: State
docs.text: Kept in <workdir>/.moraine/<file name without .toml>/: state.json (per step record), logs/<step>.log, quicklook/<step>__<output>.png. The layout of state.json is internal and may change; use moraine status FILE --json (json-output contract) to read the state.

docs.title: Contract: pyramids
docs.text: Version 1. Multi resolution copies of rasters and point clouds made by the ras-pyramid and pc-pyramid commands, read by moraine.cli.view, moraine info and moraine quicklook (decision 0007).

docs.title: Marker
docs.text:
0.zarr carries the attribute moraine_pyramid = {"version": 1, "kind": "raster" | "point cloud", "method": ..., "stats": {...}}. Readers reject versions newer than they support. Pyramids made before the marker existed are recognized by level 1 being half the size of level 0.

method (optional, absent in pyramids made before it existed) says how each level is made from the finer one: "decimate" (the default of rasters: every 2nd pixel) or "mean" (the mean of the 2 x 2 blocks over the finite pixels) for rasters, "first" (the default: the first cell with a point of each 2 x 2 block) or "mean" (the mean of the cells with points) for point clouds. A pyramid without method is decimate / first.

stats (optional, written since the statistics are computed when the pyramid is built) are the statistics of all the data (the points of a point cloud pyramid): nan_fraction, min, max, mean, std (exact), p01, p50, p99 (of a regular sample of at most 2**23 finite values) and warnings; for complex data the value fields describe the amplitude and are named amplitude_min, ...; for boolean data only true_fraction. The optional stats.zarr, shape (*channels, 8) float64 with the attribute columns (nan_fraction, min, max, mean, std, p01, p50, p99), has the same statistics of every channel (image, pair) of a stack, nan where a channel has no finite value.

docs.title: Raster pyramid (ras-pyramid)
docs.text:
<dir>/
├── 0.zarr        the raster itself, shape (nlines, width[, n])
├── 1.zarr        every 2nd pixel of 0
├── ...
├── L.zarr        L = floor(log2(min(nlines, width))), at least 2 pixels per side
└── stats.zarr    per channel statistics (see the marker above)
  • Level l has shape (ceil(nlines / 2**l), ceil(width / 2**l)[, n]). With method decimate it is ras[::2**l, ::2**l], same dtype; with method mean every cell is the mean of its 2**l x 2**l block of the data over the finite pixels (nan where all are nan; complex data averaged as complex numbers), same dtype for floating point and complex data, float32 for integer and boolean data.
  • Chunks are (chunks[0], chunks[1], 1, ...) (default (256, 256)).

docs.title: Point cloud pyramid (pc-pyramid)
docs.text:
<dir>/
├── bounds.toml   bounds = [x0, y0, xm, ym] of the rendered grid
├── x.zarr, y.zarr   coordinates of the points, (n_points,)
├── pc.zarr       the point cloud data, (n_points[, n])
├── 0.zarr ...    the points rasterized on a grid of `ras_resolution`, level l with cell size ras_resolution * 2**l
├── idx_0.zarr ...   per level, the index of the point shown in each cell, -1 for empty cells
├── rtree.zarr    bounding box tree of the points (`HilbertRtree`): (n_nodes, 4) float64, [x0, y0, xm, ym] of
│                 each node, `page_size` (points per leaf) and `n_points` in its attributes; optional, readers
│                 build it from x.zarr / y.zarr when a pyramid has none
└── stats.zarr    per channel statistics of the points (see the marker above)
  • Rows of the grid are y, columns x, like the rasters.
  • Cell (i, j) of level 0 is centred at (x0 + j * ras_resolution, y0 + i * ras_resolution) of bounds; every point is in the cell of its nearest centre and the grid reaches the cells of the largest coordinates, so bounds = [min x, min y, x0 + (width - 1) * ras_resolution, y0 + (nlines - 1) * ras_resolution] and points in different cells never share one. Pyramids made before this was fixed may have the points of the last line or column merged into the previous one.
  • Cells without points are nan in l.zarr and -1 in idx_l.zarr; the cells have the dtype of the points for floating point and complex data and are float32 for integer and boolean data.
  • idx_l keeps the first non empty cell of each 2 x 2 block for the next level. With method first, l.zarr is the value of that cell; with method mean, the mean of the non empty cells of the block (over the points of the finer levels: the mean of the points of the 2**l x 2**l block of level 0 cells).

docs.title: Design decisions
docs.text: Architecture decision records (ADR): one file per decision that shapes how moraine is built or used, with its reasons and what must not be done because of it. Agents and contributors read this index before changing the design; a decision is changed by a new record, not by editing code against it.

docs.title: Index
docs.text: # decision status 0001 Record design decisions as ADRs in docs/decisions Accepted 0002 Deep learning inference uses PyTorch only Accepted 0003 Develop moraine as a plain Python package, not with nbdev Accepted 0004 No documentation website for now Superseded by 0037 0005 The command line is generated from moraine.cli signatures and docstrings Accepted 0006 Processing chains are TOML pipelines that resume Accepted 0007 Visualization and result statistics go through pyramids Superseded by 0018 0008 Agent documentation is tool independent and tested Accepted 0009 Example pipelines are verified on real data Superseded by 0038 0010 Formats others depend on are versioned contracts Accepted 0011 The module map and layer rules are tested Accepted 0012 Redundant networks, EMCF unwrapping and time series inversion Accepted 0013 Own Delaunay triangulation and successive shortest path MCF Accepted 0014 Interactive views are generated notebooks Superseded by 0018 0015 The API layer is the package moraine.api, grouped by topic Accepted 0016 Tile viewer with anywidget and Leaflet, tiles through the notebook channel Superseded by 0018 0017 Polygons are GeoJSON files in longitude / latitude or radar grid coordinates Accepted 0018 One viewer: moraine.cli.view replaces the holoviews plots Accepted 0019 Data are chunked by blocks in space and one image per chunk Accepted 0020 EMCF on any network of image pairs, in steps of their own units Accepted 0021 Unwrapping errors are corrected by phase closure per region, as in MintPy Accepted 0022 The phase closure correction outputs the phase time series; no least squares inversion Accepted 0023 EMI regularizes coherence matrices that are not positive definite, adaptively per point Accepted 0024 Weighted DS temporal coherence with noise-free squared coherence weights Accepted 0025 The oversampling of the SLCs is measured from the speckle correlation Accepted 0026 EMI is regularized by default; DS are selected by temporal coherence Accepted 0027 Weighted temporal coherence through ds_temp_coh; no EMI quality output; speckle correlation internal Accepted 0028 DS are selected by the connectivity of the coherent image pairs, not by the number of effective pairs Accepted 0029 Compiled numba functions are cached in a directory named after the hash of the sources Accepted 0030 GPU kernels are written with numba.cuda (numba-cuda), not as cupy C++ kernels Accepted 0031 The regularized EMI on the GPU is one numba.cuda thread block per point with its matrices in shared memory Accepted 0032 Window arrays keep the whole window of a pixel in one chunk Accepted 0033 The commands run their work as tasks of an executor, not as dask array graphs Accepted 0034 The workers of the commands are moraine's own; dask is not a dependency Accepted 0035 Pyramid levels by decimation or by mean; statistics of the data computed when a pyramid is built Accepted 0036 3D views over the terrain with deck.gl and public elevation tiles Accepted 0037 The manual is a website generated from the docstrings, the command registry and docs/ Accepted 0038 The sample data set of the examples, guides and manual is Campi Flegrei Accepted

docs.title: Writing a record
docs.text:
• File name NNNN-short-title.md, the next free number; add it to the index in the same change.
  • Sections, in this order: the title line # NNNN Title, then Status, Date, Context, Decision, Consequences, Do not.
  • Status is one of Proposed, Accepted, Superseded by NNNN, Deprecated.
  • To change a decision, write a new record and mark the old one Superseded by NNNN; keep the old file.
  • Keep records short: the reason and the rule matter, the history is in git.
  • tests/test_decisions.py checks the index, the sections and the status of every record.

docs.title: 0001 Record design decisions as ADRs in docs/decisions
Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text: moraine is developed more and more with AI agents (Claude Code, Codex, ...). Decisions taken in a conversation or kept in one tool's private memory are invisible to the next session, another tool or a new contributor, which then "improves" the code back into a rejected design. moraine is small now but is expected to grow.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Every decision that shapes how moraine is built or used is written as a record in docs/decisions/, listed in docs/decisions/README.md. AGENTS.md tells agents to read the index before design changes. The format and the index are checked by tests/test_decisions.py.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Decisions travel with the code and are versioned with it.
  • A design change starts with a new record (or a superseding one), not with code.

docs.title: Do not
docs.text:
• Do not keep project decisions only in chat history, commit messages or tool-specific memory.
  • Do not delete superseded records; mark them Superseded by NNNN.

docs.title: 0002 Deep learning inference uses PyTorch only
Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
n2f, n2fs3d and n2ft ran with ONNX Runtime. Benchmarks on the sample data (634 249 points, A100):

  • ONNX Runtime CUDA fails for n2ft with more than 65 535 points (cuDNN BatchNormalization limit).
  • n2ft on CPU: 107 s with ONNX Runtime, 5.2 s with PyTorch; on GPU PyTorch works on all points (0.22 s).
  • n2f / n2fs3d (UNet): ONNX and PyTorch are about as fast; outputs agree (mean phase difference ~5e-6 rad on CPU). On GPU both differ from CPU by ~6e-4 rad because of TF32 convolutions, only at pixels where the network output is nearly zero (noise).

Keeping two inference runtimes doubles the code paths and dependencies.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: All deep learning models run with PyTorch. Models are state_dict .pth files (n2f.pth, n2fs3d.pth from github.com/kanglcn/n2f, n2ft.pth from github.com/kanglcn/n2ft) downloaded by moraine.download_dl_model(), loaded once and cached by moraine.api.dl._load_model. PyTorch is an optional dependency (pip install moraine[dl]) imported only when a model is used. cupy arrays are passed to torch with DLPack; CLI GPU workers allocate torch memory from the rmm pool. n2ft uses a fixed farthest point sampling start (start_idx=0) so results are reproducible.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• onnxruntime is no longer a dependency; import moraine does not import torch.
  • TF32 stays enabled on GPU (5x faster than strict FP32 for the UNet); results differ slightly from CPU.

docs.title: Do not
docs.text:
• Do not add ONNX Runtime or another inference runtime back.
  • Do not import torch at module level in code that import moraine loads.
  • Do not change the model architectures in moraine/api/unet_torch_.py / moraine/api/n2ft_torch_.py without new weights: they must match the published .pth files.

docs.title: 0003 Develop moraine as a plain Python package, not with nbdev
Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text: moraine was written with nbdev: the source was in notebooks, exported to .py. Tests only ran as notebooks (several passed only because of notebook globals and hid real bugs), parameter docs were inline comments that tools could not read, and packaging was split over settings.ini and setup.py.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: The .py files in moraine/ are the source. Packaging is pyproject.toml (PEP 621). Functions have numpy style docstrings. Tests are pytest in tests/, skipping what needs the sample data, a GPU, GAMMA or the models. The API / CLI notebooks were removed; tutorial notebooks stay in nbs/Tutorials.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Porting the notebook tests found and fixed bugs (CPU ad_intf_pc, isPD / nearestPD on numpy, HilbertRtree.save / load, is_cuda_available).
  • Docstrings are also the input of the command line help (see 0005).

docs.title: Do not
docs.text:
• Do not reintroduce nbdev (nbdev_export would overwrite the source) or code generated from notebooks.
  • Do not put tests in notebooks; tutorials are examples, not tests.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Superseded by 0037

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The Quarto website was built by nbdev from the API notebooks, which no longer exist (0003).

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: No documentation website is maintained for now. Documentation is: docstrings (help(), moraine COMMAND --help), README.md, AGENTS.md, docs/workflows/, docs/decisions/ and the tutorial notebooks.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: • The deploy workflow and the Quarto configuration were removed.

docs.title: Do not
docs.text: • Do not add a documentation generator or website without a new decision record.

docs.title: 0005 The command line is generated from moraine.cli signatures and docstrings
Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text: AI agents and scripts need a command line with complete help and machine readable output. Writing the commands by hand would duplicate every function signature and drift from the code.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Every @mc_logger function in moraine/cli/ is a moraine sub command (moraine/command/). Options, types and help come from the signature and the numpy docstring, so the docstrings are the specification: shapes, dtypes, input or output and real defaults must be exact. Unknown argument names are errors with a suggestion; extra keyword arguments must be explicit (--kw / [step.kw]). Tuple arguments are validated (tuple[int, int] needs two integers). --json prints one JSON object on stdout, logs go to stderr.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Adding a CLI function adds a command; tests/test_command.py checks that every argument is documented.
  • A wrong docstring is a user-facing bug.

docs.title: Do not
docs.text:
• Do not hand-write argument parsing for individual commands.
  • Do not let unknown arguments pass silently into **kwargs.
  • Do not print anything but the JSON result on stdout with --json.

docs.title: 0006 Processing chains are TOML pipelines that resume
Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text: A processing chain has tens of steps, takes hours on real data and is tuned by rerunning parts of it. Agents need to change parameters without writing code and resume after failures.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Processing chains are TOML files run by moraine run (moraine/command/pipeline.py): [vars] with ${name} (overridable with --var), [defaults], [[step]] with a command and its arguments. A step is skipped when its argument hash and the modification times of its inputs are unchanged; steps downstream of a changed output rerun. State, logs and quicklooks are kept per pipeline file in <workdir>/.moraine/<file name>/.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Several pipeline files can share a working directory and read each other's outputs.
  • moraine status / --dry-run explain what will run and why.

docs.title: Do not
docs.text:
• Do not keep processing state elsewhere than .moraine/<file name>/.
  • Do not make a step depend on anything but its arguments and input files.

docs.title: 0007 Visualization and result statistics go through pyramids
Status
docs.text: Superseded by 0018

docs.title: Context
docs.text: moraine is made for data larger than memory. zarr reads whole chunks, so strided sampling of a large array still reads every chunk. moraine already has pyramids (ras-pyramid, pc-pyramid) and plots that read the level matching the view (ras_plot, pc_plot, holoviews).

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• moraine info shows metadata only for plain arrays (no data read).
  • For pyramids it adds statistics from the finest level of at most 64 MiB (a regular decimation of the scene) and warnings for all-nan, infinite and constant values; point cloud pyramids skip empty cells.
  • moraine quicklook only accepts pyramids and draws them with ras_plot / pc_plot, saved with the holoviews matplotlib backend (no browser needed).
  • pc_plot builds its rtree lazily so overviews do not read all coordinates.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Results worth checking get a pyramid step in the pipelines.
  • Checking a result costs the same for any data size.

docs.title: Do not
docs.text:
• Do not write custom sampling, statistics over full arrays or custom plotting code for checks.
  • Do not read whole arrays to inspect results.

docs.title: 0008 Agent documentation is tool independent and tested
Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Users drive moraine with different AI tools (Claude Code, Codex, DeepSeek through Cursor / Cline). Documentation that drifts from the code misleads agents more than no documentation.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: AGENTS.md is the entry point for all agents; docs/workflows/ has one guide per example pipeline with expected result ranges. Tool specific files only point to them: CLAUDE.md is @AGENTS.md, .claude/skills/ are thin wrappers. tests/test_docs.py checks that documented commands and files exist and that the example pipelines parse.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: • One set of instructions for every tool.

docs.title: Do not
docs.text:
• Do not put instructions only in a tool specific file (CLAUDE.md, skills, .cursor/, ...).
  • Do not document commands, files or numbers that were not checked against the code or a real run.

docs.title: 0009 Example pipelines are verified on real data
Status
docs.text: Superseded by 0038

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Agents start from examples. An example that was never run spreads its errors; running the chain end to end also finds bugs that unit tests miss.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: examples/*.toml cover the whole chain (load, PS, DS, refinement, unwrapping) and are run end to end on the sample data (data/gamma, 2500 x 1834 x 17) before they change. The numbers in docs/workflows/ (counts, ranges, run times) come from such a run.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: • The first full run (commit 85c2139) found four bugs (missing parent directories in load-gamma-*, image pair files read too early, stdout pollution of moraine run --json, per-chunk directories taken for pyramids).

docs.title: Do not
docs.text:
• Do not add or change an example without running it, and update the guide numbers from that run.
  • Do not copy parameters into the guides that the examples do not use.

docs.title: 0010 Formats others depend on are versioned contracts
Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Agents and scripts parse the --json output, users keep pipeline files and pyramids for a long time, and every stored result follows the data conventions. When these change silently, old files and scripts break without a clear error, and nobody can tell which behaviour is intended.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: The --json output, pipeline files, pyramids and data conventions are specified in docs/contracts/. The first three carry a version (JSON_VERSION, PIPELINE_VERSION, PYRAMID_VERSION) written into the output or file; readers reject newer versions with a clear error. tests/test_contracts.py compares the documented fields and layouts with the real outputs.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• A change to these formats changes the contract and its tests in the same commit.
  • Writing the contract tests found two bugs: outputs named without / or . were not detected, and a failed moraine run raised SystemExit from main().

docs.title: Do not
docs.text:
• Do not add, rename or remove a field of the --json output without updating docs/contracts/json-output.md.
  • Do not make a breaking change without bumping the version and recording the decision.

docs.title: 0011 The module map and layer rules are tested
Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text: moraine will grow. Agents and new contributors need to know where code goes before changing it, and a hand written map goes stale unless something checks it.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: ARCHITECTURE.md lists every module of moraine/ with its responsibility and states the dependency rules between the API, CLI and command layers. tests/test_architecture.py fails when a module is missing from the map, the map names a module that does not exist, a layer imports a higher one, or import moraine imports torch. docs/development.md describes how changes are made and validated.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: • Adding, moving or removing a module needs an ARCHITECTURE.md update in the same change.

docs.title: Do not
docs.text:
• Do not import moraine.cli or moraine.command from the API layer, or moraine.command from the CLI layer.
  • Do not work around the architecture test by adding exceptions; propose a new record instead.

docs.title: 0012 Redundant networks, EMCF unwrapping and time series inversion
Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
moraine stops at unwrapping. mcf_pc unwraps every interferogram separately (2D) on a Delaunay triangulation of the grid indices, with unit costs, the first point as implicit reference and no quality output. The example unwraps sequential pairs only (bandwidth 1): n - 1 interferograms for n - 1 unknowns, so unwrapping errors cannot be detected.

After phase linking, the wrapped phase history is consistent in time (zero wrapped closure), so a redundant network adds information only against unwrapping errors. Redundancy serves two purposes: temporal unwrapping (EMCF) and a least squares inversion whose residuals measure unwrapping quality.

Reference implementations (isce-framework, reviewed 2026-09-28):

  • spurt (workflows/emcf): EMCF on sparse points. Temporal step: for each spatial Delaunay edge, the wrapped gradients of all interferograms are summed around the triangles of the interferogram network in time - perpendicular baseline space and an MCF on that temporal network corrects them. Spatial step: per interferogram, MCF on the spatial triangulation with the corrected gradients, then flood fill. Costs: constant, distance or centroid.
  • dolphin (timeseries.py): incidence matrix without the first date; L2 by batched least squares, weighted by the Cramer-Rao bound (1 - g^2) / (2 L g^2); L1 by ADMM (20 iterations, cached Cholesky of A^T A); missing / unreliable data masked per pixel; residuals per date as quality; linear velocity by weighted polyfit. Reference point: centroid of the largest high quality region.

moraine's mcf_pc already is the spatial step of EMCF (Delaunay, dual graph MCF with OR-Tools, integration). meta.toml has dates, perpendicular baselines and pixel spacings.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Extend the chain after phase linking in five stages, each a complete change (API function, CLI command, docstring, tests, example and guide):

  1. Network: TempNet.from_delaunay(dates, bperp, ...): Delaunay triangulation of the images in (time, perpendicular baseline) space, normalized by user scales, optionally limited by maximum temporal / perpendicular baseline; it also returns the triangles (temporal cycles). The image-pairs command gets a meta input and a delaunay method.
  2. Spatial MCF improvements (mcf_pc, output unchanged): coordinates scaled by the pixel spacings (or map coordinates), and edge costs constant (current behaviour, default) or distance.
  3. EMCF (emcf_pc, command emcf-pc; its network and the split into steps are changed by decision 0020): inputs point coordinates, the wrapped phase history (n_points, nimages) and the network; output unwrapped phase (n_points, n_image_pairs) float32, same layout as mcf_pc. Temporal MCFs are many and small: batched over spatial edges, parallel.
  4. Inversion (invert_pc, command ts-inversion-pc; not implemented, replaced by the image phases of the phase closure correction, decision 0022): unwrapped phase (n_points, n_image_pairs) and image pairs -> phase time series (n_points, nimages) float32 radians relative to the first image, plus the residual per point (n_points,) as quality. Methods l2 (optionally weighted) and l1 (ADMM as in dolphin: cached Cholesky of A^T A, fixed iterations, batched over points; robust to single unwrapping errors; chosen over IRLS, whose per point weights prevent batching). Points processed in chunks, numpy / cupy. A single reference network (no redundancy) is copied, not inverted.
  5. Products (separate record when started): reference point, velocity (linear, optional annual terms) with uncertainty, DEM error, stratified atmosphere and ramps, LOS decomposition, export (CSV / GeoPackage / GeoTIFF).

The residual of stage 4 gets a pyramid in the example, so moraine info reports its statistics and agents can detect unwrapping problems. New array layouts are added to docs/contracts/data.md when their stage is implemented.

Validation per stage: synthetic data with known deformation and injected 2 pi errors (the network / EMCF / L1 must detect or remove them), the sample data (examples/05_unwrap.toml extended or a new 06_*.toml), and rewrapping the result must give the input phase.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• mcf_pc and gamma_mcf_pt stay; EMCF is an alternative for redundant networks.
  • Stages 1-4 need no new dependencies (scipy Delaunay, OR-Tools, numba / cupy).
  • Stages are done in order; stage 2 is a separate change, reused by the spatial step of EMCF.
  • examples/05_unwrap.toml switches from sequential pairs + mcf-pc to a Delaunay network, EMCF and the inversion once stages 3 and 4 work (one standard chain, no separate example).

docs.title: Do not
docs.text:
• Do not invert a network without redundancy and report its residual as a quality measure: it is zero by construction.
  • Do not change the output layout of mcf_pc / gamma_mcf_pt.
  • Do not add external data dependencies (weather models, TEC maps) in stages 1-4.

docs.title: 0013 Own Delaunay triangulation and successive shortest path MCF
Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
mcf_pc used scipy's Qhull triangulation and OR-Tools' min cost flow. Measured on 10 million points (synthetic, known truth): Qhull 101 s, edge extraction (np.unique) 9 s, OR-Tools 73-170 s depending on the edge order, integration 6 s, peak memory about 3.5 GB above the data; GAMMA mcf_pt takes 35 s. Qhull breaks cocircular ties (frequent on the integer grid of radar coordinates) by input order, so results depended on the point order; OR-Tools' solution among equal cost optima too.

Residues usually pair with close neighbours, which suits successive shortest paths (SSP, also used by GAMMA): each Dijkstra stops at the nearest sink and stays local.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• moraine/api/unwrap/delaunay_.py: own sweep-hull triangulation (following Delaunator, ISC license, notice in the file) with exact integer predicates and coordinate based tie breaking, returning half-edges.
